trace_issues.message: After COPY DBTBLS REPLACING, two 01 items carry the name WS-ERRLOG-REC (the enclosing 01 at line 18 and the renamed copybook record ERRLOG-RECORD). resolve-field-references returned RESOLVED to the program record SYS-PORTFOLIO-001-FIL-0056-REC-0001 (registry names differ); which item INITIALIZE (line 73) and the host variable :WS-ERRLOG-REC (line 129) address at compile time is flagged for SME review.
Static CALL 'ERRPROC' USING ERR-MESSAGE; ERRPROC is a separate program (not in this execution's scope); its effect is not traced here.

program_narrative: Program DB2ERR is a called DB2 error-handling subroutine that receives a request block LS-ERROR-REQUEST (PROCEDURE DIVISION USING) and dispatches on its function code. 'LOG ' builds an error-log row (timestamp, calling program ID, error type 'D', severity derived from the SQLCODE, a text 'SQLCODE: ... STATE: ...', the caller's error text, process date/time and additional info) and inserts it into the DB2 table ERRLOG; the severity step also sets the caller's retry flag to 'Y' for deadlock (-911) or timeout (-913) and 'N' otherwise. 'DIAG' returns a diagnostic message and return code for the SQLCODE (deadlock/timeout 4, connection error -30081 12, duplicate key -803 8, other negative 12, other non-negative 4). 'RETR' selects the latest ERRLOG row for the given program ID and returns its message and severity, or 'No error history found' with return code 4. Any other function code, and a failed ERRLOG insert, set return code 12 and call the external error processor ERRPROC with the common ERR-MESSAGE block. It reads no files and always ends with GOBACK.

paragraphs.name: 1100-SET-SEVERITY
pseudocode: SELECT CASE request.sqlcode  -- EVALUATE LS-SQLCODE against the WS-ERROR-CATEGORIES constants
SET request.retry_flag = 'Y'  -- LS-SHOULD-RETRY: caller may retry
paragraphs.pseudocode_text:
SELECT CASE request.sqlcode  -- EVALUATE LS-SQLCODE against the WS-ERROR-CATEGORIES constants
  WHEN -911 (deadlock, WS-DEADLOCK), -913 (timeout, WS-TIMEOUT):
    SET errlog.error_severity = 2  -- EL-SEV-WARN
    SET request.retry_flag = 'Y'  -- LS-SHOULD-RETRY: caller may retry
  WHEN -30081 (connection error, WS-CONNECTION-ERROR):
    SET errlog.error_severity = 4  -- EL-SEV-SEVERE
    SET request.retry_flag = 'N'  -- LS-NO-RETRY
  WHEN -803 (duplicate key, WS-DUP-KEY):
    SET errlog.error_severity = 1  -- EL-SEV-INFO
    SET request.retry_flag = 'N'  -- LS-NO-RETRY
  WHEN +100 (not found, WS-NOT-FOUND):
    SET errlog.error_severity = 1  -- EL-SEV-INFO
    SET request.retry_flag = 'N'  -- LS-NO-RETRY
  ELSE:
    IF request.sqlcode < 0 THEN
      SET errlog.error_severity = 3  -- EL-SEV-ERROR
      SET request.retry_flag = 'N'  -- LS-NO-RETRY
    ELSE
      SET errlog.error_severity = 1  -- EL-SEV-INFO
      SET request.retry_flag = 'N'  -- LS-NO-RETRY
    END IF
END SELECT

annotations.note: The WHEN objects are WORKING-STORAGE constants with VALUE clauses (WS-DEADLOCK -911, WS-TIMEOUT -913, WS-CONNECTION-ERROR -30081, WS-DUP-KEY -803, WS-NOT-FOUND +100); no statement in the program changes them.
WHEN WS-DEADLOCK immediately followed by WHEN WS-TIMEOUT: both values share the same body (lines 104-105).

paragraphs.name: 2000-DIAGNOSE-ERROR
pseudocode: SET request.error_text = 'DB2 connection error - check availability'
ELSE:  -- also reached for +100 (not found): this EVALUATE has no WHEN WS-NOT-FOUND
paragraphs.pseudocode_text:
SELECT CASE request.sqlcode
  WHEN -911 (deadlock, WS-DEADLOCK):
    SET request.error_text = 'Deadlock detected - retry transaction'
    SET request.return_code = 4
  WHEN -913 (timeout, WS-TIMEOUT):
    SET request.error_text = 'Timeout occurred - retry transaction'
    SET request.return_code = 4
  WHEN -30081 (connection error, WS-CONNECTION-ERROR):
    SET request.error_text = 'DB2 connection error - check availability'
    SET request.return_code = 12
  WHEN -803 (duplicate key, WS-DUP-KEY):
    SET request.error_text = 'Duplicate key violation'
    SET request.return_code = 8
  ELSE:  -- also reached for +100 (not found): this EVALUATE has no WHEN WS-NOT-FOUND
    IF request.sqlcode < 0 THEN
      SET request.error_text = 'Unhandled DB2 error'
      SET request.return_code = 12
    ELSE
      SET request.error_text = 'DB2 warning condition'
      SET request.return_code = 4
    END IF
END SELECT

annotations.note: Unlike 1100-SET-SEVERITY, this EVALUATE has no WHEN WS-NOT-FOUND; SQLCODE +100 is handled by WHEN OTHER and, being non-negative, yields 'DB2 warning condition' with return code 4.
The DIAG function does not change the retry flag LS-RETRY-FLAG; only the LOG path (1100-SET-SEVERITY) sets it.
